assumptions: Floor request inputs PS1/PS2/PS3 and arrival sensing inputs S1/S2/S3 are modeled as discrete events because the NL describes them as triggers and arrivals, and no persistent input variables or simultaneous event/guard semantics were specified.

The hbrg encoding is hbrg = 1 for upward drive, hbrg = -1 for downward drive, and hbrg = 0 for stop; numeric values were chosen because the NL requires distinctions but does not specify exact signal values.

The phrase immediately checks the next destination is represented by entering a floor state that can accept the next request event; no additional decision or junction states were added because the NL did not list such states or priority rules.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init dispatches to F1 stopped, then PS2 moves upward to MU2, S2 stops at F2, and the next PS3 request immediately moves upward to MU3.
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_to_f2_then_up_to_f3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F1 checks PS3 selects MU3, S3 stops at F3, then PS2 selects downward MD2 and S2 stops at F2.
scenario_results.name: f1_direct_to_f3_then_down_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F2 checks PS1 selects downward MD1 and S1 arrival stops at F1.
scenario_results.name: f2_down_request_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F3 checks PS1 selects MD1, then Reset from a downward motion context forces F1 stopped.
scenario_results.name: f3_down_request_reset_from_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F2 verifies the global Reset also forces F1 from a stopped floor context.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_floor_context

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from MU3 verifies Reset forces F1 from an upward drive context and clears hbrg to stop.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_upward_motion_context

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes absence of phantom transitions: F1 stays stopped with no request, and MU2 remains upward motion without S2 arrival.
scenario_results.name: no_fire_without_request_or_sensor

evidence: NL requires states F1/F2/F3 and MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL transitions F1+PS2->MU2, F1+PS3->MU3, F2+PS3->MU3, F2+PS1->MD1, F3+PS1->MD1, F3+PS2->MD2 are all present.
NL arrival transitions MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, MD2+S2->F2 are all present.
DSL has [*] -> F1 and ! * -> F1 :: Reset, matching initial F1 and global reset requirements.
hbrg is set to 1 in upward motion states, -1 in downward motion states, and 0 in floor states.
findings.summary: The DSL closely follows the NL elevator FSM: all named floor states, motion states, request-triggered dispatch transitions, arrival-sensor transitions, initial F1 state, reset-to-F1 behavior, and hbrg drive/stop distinctions are represented.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary lists W_UNREFERENCED_VAR: Variable 'hbrg' does not affect any transition guard.
NL identifies hbrg as an output distinguishing upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
The variable is assigned in state entry actions and is intentionally not used as transition state memory or guard input.
findings.summary: The diagnostic W_UNREFERENCED_VAR on hbrg is expected for an output-only signal and should not be treated as evidence that hbrg needs to affect guards. If the DSL supports explicit output declarations, hbrg could be modeled as a pure output rather than a generic int variable.

No-fire scenario checks F1 without request and MU2 without S2 arrival.
findings.summary: No material coverage gap found for the stated NL behavior. The tests exercise representative upward, downward, arrival, reset, and no-phantom-transition paths.
